chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Himmani who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Hisham ibn al-Hakam has alleged that God is a body; there is nothing resembling Him — All-knowing, Hearing, Seeing, Powerful, a Speaker, and articulate — and that Speech, Power, and Knowledge flow as one flow, none of them being created.'

So he said: 'May God destroy him! Does he not know that the body is limited, and speech is other than the speaker? I seek refuge in God and disavow before God this statement. There is neither body, nor image, nor limitation, and everything besides Him is created. Things come into being only by His Will and His Decree, without speech, without hesitation in Himself, and without articulation by a tongue.'

key_terms.إِرَادَة: Will (irada) — God's volitional act of creation, distinct from human speech or deliberation.
key_terms.تَحْدِيد: Delimitation/limitation — assigning spatial or conceptual limits to God, categorically denied.
key_terms.جِسْم: Body — a corporeal, bounded entity. The claim that God is a body (tajsim) was a major theological controversy in early Islam.
key_terms.مَحْدُود: Limited/bounded — a key theological argument: whatever has limits is contingent and cannot be God.
key_terms.مَشِيئَة: Desire/Decree (mashia) — God's creative will, synonymous with but distinct from irada in Shia kalam.
key_terms.مَعَاذَ اللَّه: I seek refuge in God — an expression of horror at a blasphemous statement.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kazim say about the claim that God is a body?
ai.summary: Al-Hasan al-Himmani reported to Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) that Hisham ibn al-Hakam, a prominent Shia theologian, had claimed that God is a body (though unlike any other body) and that God's attributes of Speech, Power, and Knowledge are uncreated and flow as one. The Imam responded with sharp rebuke, declaring: the body is inherently limited — a concept incompatible with God — and that speech is distinct from the one who speaks. The Imam emphatically declared God to be free of body, form, and limitation, affirming instead that all things are created by divine Will alone, without speech or inner deliberation. This hadith reflects the second/eighth-century theological debates in Kufa surrounding divine attributes (sifat), particularly the question of whether the divine attributes (kalam, qudra, 'ilm) are eternal or created. The Imam's position aligned with the transcendentalist (tanzih) strand of Shia theology.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Abbas, from Al Hassan Bin Abdul Rahman Al Himmany who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan Musa Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that Hisham Bin Al-Hakam is alleging that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is a body. There is nothing resembling Him<sup>azwj</sup>. All-knowing, Hearing, Seeing, Powerful. A Speaker speaking, and the Speech, and the Power, and the Knowledge, (all) flowing as one flow, there being nothing from it being Created’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Kill him! Does he not know that the body is limited, and the speech is other than the speaker? I<sup>asws</sup> seek Refuge of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I keep away from this speech. There is neither a body, nor an image, nor a limitation, and everything Besides Him<sup>azwj</sup> is a creation. But rather, the things came to be by His<sup>azwj</sup> Will, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Desire from without a speech, or hesitation in Himself<sup>azwj</sup>, or speaking by a tongue’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn abu ‘Abdallah has narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Ali ibn al-‘Abbass from al-Hassan ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Hammani who has said the following.

“I said to abu al-Hassan Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s.), ‘Hisham ibn al-Hakam claims that Allah is a body like unto Whom there is no one. He is All-knowing, All-hearing, All-seeing, All-powerful. He speaks and reasons. His word, His power, His knowledge are all in one. No one of them is created.’”

The Imam said, “May Allah be his foe. Does he not know that the body is limited, and that the speech is other than what the speaker is? I seek refuge from Allah and I disclaim such words. Allah does not have a body, form or any kind of limitations. Allah has created everything. He creates things as and when He wills without any word or planing in the mind or utterance of the tongue.”
